references.text: The original account of when Moses burned the golden calf, ground it to dust, and scattered it on water that the Israelites had to drink.
Moses' anger when he came down from the mountain and saw the golden calf and the dancing, which led to the destruction of the calf.
The account of how Aaron made the golden calf that the people worshiped, the same sin Moses refers to here.
The full account of the making of the golden calf while Moses was on the mountain, which is the background for this sin.
Moses' earlier mention in the same chapter of how the people sinned by making a golden calf, a cast idol.
The psalmist's poetic description of how Israel made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast image, exchanging their glory.
Stephen's reference in his speech to when the Israelites made a calf and rejoiced over the work of their hands.
Nehemiah's prayer that mentions the golden calf as a great sin the people committed in the wilderness.
